lock.hypothesis: At 30/90/180-day horizons AWS GPU spot prices are regime-driven (AI demand build-out vs capacity ramp), so the seed's fixed 730-day pooled change quantiles are stale: measured mean bias is -0.03/-0.16/-0.30 (log) at h30/90/180 with q90 breach 27%. Blending recent-180d change quantiles (w=0.5) and adding a capped cross-sectional mean-reversion shift (AZs below their instance-type median revert up; corr(fwd, csmed-level) = +0.26/+0.44/+0.57) at h>=90 only raises the center and upper band into the prevailing regime, cutting the long-horizon bias and q90 breaches. Both levers are gated OFF at h30, where the dense backtest showed them loss-negative (-0.012/-0.055).

hypothesis_card.mechanism: Recent-window (180d) empirical h-day log-change quantiles track the prevailing drift regime (2023-24: rising AI demand, measured recent-180d h180 q50 +0.65 vs 730d 0.0 at 2024-09), and AZs priced below their instance-type cross-sectional median revert upward (corr +0.57 at h180). Both shift the whole quantile triple up, reducing the -0.30 h180 center bias and the 34% q90 breach that dominate the pooled loss.
hypothesis_card.expected_observation: Discovery pooled skill rises from 0.2450 to ~0.273 with the h180 slice improving most (+0.051 skill, coverage +0.008) and h90 slightly (+0.008); h30 unchanged (gated). Dense backtest shows h180 +0.040 skill with the p5 (H100) series most helped and no horizon regressing.
hypothesis_card.competing_explanation: The gain is not regime adaptation but pure variance reduction from averaging two noisy quantile estimates (730d and 180d windows), which would also appear when blending two arbitrary windows and would not be specific to the rising-demand regime; alternatively the 2023-24 Discovery uptrend makes ANY upward center shift look good in-sample while adding no out-of-sample information (the champion's center is in-sample-optimal by construction).
hypothesis_card.test: Paired comparison vs the seed champion on the 16 Discovery origins (dry run) and a dense 33-origin stride-14 backtest inside Discovery, decomposing per-horizon deltas: the blend-only backtest isolated the recent-window lever (h180 +0.040, h30 -0.012) and the dry run isolated the CS-shift contribution (h90 -0.015 -> +0.008 with shift on), which motivated the h>=90 gate.
hypothesis_card.rejection_condition: Rejected if Discovery pooled skill <= champion (0.2450) or any sanity check fails; the regime hypothesis is falsified if the h180 gain disappears out of sample (Holdout h180 skill <= champion's 0.3551) or if the recent-window blend is loss-positive at h90/h180 on the dense backtest (it was +0.040 at h180, -0.015 at h90 before gating).

lock.market_insight: The forecast assumes AWS GPU spot prices over 30-180 days are driven by the generative-AI capacity cycle rather than short-term momentum: H100 (p5) demand outstripping supply keeps a positive drift on premium instances, while older-generation A100 (p4d) capacity gradually migrates to H100/H200 fleets, leaving AZ-level discounts to mean-revert toward the instance-type median. Dated evidence from point-in-time searches: Liftr Insights (2024-05-29, prnewswire.com/news-releases/ai-accelerator-prices-rising-but-its-good-for-users-302157388.html) verifies a 12.2% 3-year rise in AI cloud compute prices; Shadeform (2024-01-20, shadeform.com/resources/articles/nvidia-a100-gpus-a-cost-and-availability-analysis) documents Lambda Labs' largest price increase and the A100-to-H100 market shift; Aaron Ginn (2024-02-07, linkedin.com/pulse/month-gpus-february-2024) notes H100 prices stabilizing after 2023's increase with supply shortages easing; TechCrunch (2024-05-05) and NextPlatform (2024-05-02) document hyperscaler H100 allocations (AWS ~50K) and alternative-cloud price pressure. A web-news drift gate built on these signals was tested and never fired on Discovery (all age-gated articles were direction-mixed), so the committed forecast is pack-only; the regime signal is captured instead by the recent-180d empirical change quantiles. The view would change if forward prices fell while the recent window showed gains (capacity build-out catching up, e.g. broad H200/GB200 availability or a demand shock), or if AZ-level dispersion stopped reverting (persistent regional allocation shifts).

lock.hypothesis: At 30/90/180-day horizons, AWS GPU spot prices are administered around an instance-family level: AZs priced BELOW their family cross-sectional median level revert UP toward it over 90-180 days (AWS compresses spot discounts and rebalances reclaimed capacity across AZs), so shifting the whole quantile triple of below-median AZs up toward the family median (weight 0.5 at h90, 0.7 at h180, clip 0.5 log) cuts the long-horizon pinball loss that the seed's pure last-value x pooled-change-quantile forecast leaves on the table. Above-median AZs are left untouched (down-shift measured Discovery-negative, -0.019 h180) and h30 is gated off (measured loss-negative).

hypothesis_card.mechanism: Within an AWS instance family (p4d/p5/...), spot prices across AZs share an administered level set by AWS's spot-pricing algorithm; AZ-level deviations are transient capacity artifacts (reclaimed Capacity Blocks, regional demand spikes). Over 90-180 days the below-median AZs converge up (measured on 2023-06..2024-03 pseudo-origins: up-only shift h180 +0.063 / h90 +0.055 skill vs seed, positive in 7/10 origins, and beating both constant uplift +0.027 and the symmetric form), so adding clip(diff, 0, 0.5) * w (w=0.5 at h90, 0.7 at h180) to the seed's pooled 730-day change quantiles reduces the q50/q90 under-forecast on cheap AZs.
hypothesis_card.expected_observation: Discovery pooled skill rises from 0.2450 to ~0.267 (+0.022), with h180 +0.026 and h90 +0.027, h30 unchanged (gated); coverage_80 rises ~+0.022 (fewer q90 breaches on below-median series); median skill +0.017. Dense backtest: pooled +0.022 with z >> 2, ~2/3 of origins improved, helped series concentrated in below-median p4d AZs (use2-az2, apne1-az4, usw2-az3).
hypothesis_card.competing_explanation: The gain is not cross-sectional mean reversion but a generic upward center shift that happens to look good in the 2023-24 AI-demand Discovery window (any uplift would score well while prices rose); alternatively it is pure variance reduction from shrinking the gap to the family median. Evidence against the rival: constant uplift (+0.10/+0.20 log) scored only +0.027 h180 vs up_only's +0.063 on the same pseudo-origins, and the down-only direction was Discovery-NEGATIVE (-0.019 h180, dry run 1) — a generic "prices rose" artifact would have rewarded both directions.
hypothesis_card.test: Paired dry run on the 16 Discovery origins (pooled +0.0225, 10/16 origins improved, h90 +0.027 / h180 +0.026, coverage +0.022) plus a dense 33-origin stride-14 backtest inside Discovery (pooled delta +0.0219, origin-bootstrap SE 0.0027, z = 8.0, 64% of origins improved, helped cells concentrated in below-median p4d AZs, worst regression -0.003 on a single p5 series). The direction was decided by a pseudo-origin scan restricted to the scored window after the down-only variant failed the screen (-0.009 pooled).
hypothesis_card.rejection_condition: Rejected if Discovery pooled skill <= champion (0.2450) or any sanity check fails (final: 0.2675, screen PASS). The reversion hypothesis is falsified if the h90/h180 gains do not transfer out of sample (Holdout h90 <= 0.2150 or h180 <= 0.3551, the champion's values) or if the dense backtest delta is not significant (|z| < 2); measured z = 8.0, so only a Holdout reversal would falsify it.

lock.market_insight: The forecast assumes AWS GPU spot prices over 90-180 days are administered around an instance-family level rather than drifting freely per AZ: AWS actively manages spot pricing to keep it attractive (re:Invent 2024 capacity-management recap, zenn.dev/articles/831696491092b17: "there has been a significant drop [in Spot prices] over the past year. We continue to look for ways to lower these prices further"), and Capacity Blocks for ML (AWS News Blog, 2023-10-31, aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/announcing-amazon-ec2-capacity-blocks-for-ml) reclaim idle GPU capacity so under-used AZs do not stay cheap forever — both forces pull below-median AZs back toward the family median, which is the direction the committed shift encodes. The AI-demand context (NextPlatform 2024-05-02 H100 allocation data; TechSpot 2024-02-27 on easing H100 lead times) supports premium-family (p5) prices staying elevated while older p4d capacity is repriced. The view would change if AWS stopped compressing spot discounts (e.g. a broad spot price INCREASE leaving below-median AZs persistently cheap), if a new generation (p6/Blackwell) made current p5/p4d capacity structurally obsolete and monotonically cheaper, or if the dense backtest's below-median reversion gain failed to transfer to the 2025 Holdout window.
